title: How much learning does it take to survive a change: evolutionary rescue by standing variation in learning rate, and a milder change that is harder to survive. A preregistered artificial-life experiment (mini-world, protocol N4-v1)
description:
Report, preregistration, code and raw data of protocol N4-v1 of the mini-world (minimir) project, a small artificial-life world for preregistered experiments on the evolution of learning. A population of simple learning agents faces one abrupt reversal of which of two food colours is nutritious and which is poisonous. Each of 150 worlds was run once up to the tick before the reversal and then copied 26 times, each copy receiving a single intervention on the learning rate of its individuals, on the spread of that rate, or on the strength of the poison. The outcome is survival of the population 12,000 ticks later. Four criteria and one validity check were frozen on 20 November 2026, before the first confirmatory run, after each had been tested on synthetic data with and without an effect.

Results: two hypotheses confirmed, one undetermined. A spread of learning rates rescues populations whose median individual learns too slowly (0 of 150 worlds survive with no spread, 134 of 150 with the widest; difference 0.893, 95% CI 0.840 to 0.940). A milder poison rescues fewer worlds, the opposite of what classical rescue theory predicts (0.445 against 0.582 on middle rates; difference -0.137, 95% CI -0.170 to -0.105). That each world has its own threshold stayed undetermined under the declared rule. With learning switched off no world survived. The report is REPORT_N4_EN.md (English) and REPORT_N4.md (Russian); the frozen preregistration is PREREGISTRATION_N4.md; raw results are in runs/n4/protocol_n4.jsonl and the single reading in runs/n4/reading_n4.json.

This release also contains the earlier closed protocols of the project: protocol B1-100k-v1 (report REPORT_B_EN.md, erratum of 28 October 2026) and protocol A.

Page of the experiment: https://minimir.ilinmaks.com/n4.html
notes: Protocol N4-v1 is closed: frozen on 20 November 2026 (commit 944e88d), computed and read once on 21 November 2026 (commit 9f1706e). Report texts, preregistrations and data in runs/ are CC BY 4.0, see LICENSE. Protocol B1-100k-v1 remains archived as version 1.0.1-protocol-b, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23729180.
